Horizon Bancorp, Inc. ("Horizon" or the "Company") is a registered bank holding company incorporated in Indiana and headquartered in Michigan City, Indiana. Horizon provides a broad range of banking services in northern and central Indiana and southern and central Michigan through its bank subsidiary, Horizon Bank ("Horizon Bank" or the "Bank") and other affiliated entities. Horizon operates as a single segment, which is commercial banking. Horizon's common stock is traded on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol HBNC. Horizon Bank (formerly known as "Horizon Bank, N.A.") was founded in 1873 as a national association, and it remained a national association until its conversion to an Indiana commercial bank effective June 23, 2017. The Bank is a full–service commercial bank offering commercial and retail banking services, corporate and individual trust and agency services and other services incident to banking.

Over the last 20 years, Horizon has expanded its geographic reach and experienced financial growth through a combination of both organic expansion and mergers and acquisitions. Horizon's initial operations focused on northwest Indiana, but since then, the Company has developed a presence in new markets in southern and central Michigan and northeastern and central Indiana.

The Bank maintains 71 full service offices. At December 31, 2025, the Bank had total assets of $6.4 billion and total deposits of $5.3 billion. The Bank has wholly–owned direct and indirect subsidiaries: Horizon Investments, Inc. ("Horizon Investments"), Horizon Properties, Inc. ("Horizon Properties"), Horizon Insurance Services, Inc. ("Horizon Insurance"), Horizon Grantor Trust and Wolverine Commercial Holdings, LLC. Horizon Investments manages the investment portfolio of the Bank. Horizon Properties manages the real estate investment trust. Horizon Insurance is used by the Company's Wealth Management to sell certain life insurance products through a third party. Horizon Grantor Trust holds title to certain company owned life insurance policies. Wolverine Commercial Holdings, LLC currently holds one piece of property but does not otherwise engage in significant business activities.

Horizon formed Horizon Bancorp Capital Trust II in 2004 ("Trust II") and Horizon Bancorp Capital Trust III in 2006 ("Trust III") for the purpose of participating in pooled trust preferred securities offerings. The Company assumed additional debentures as the result of the acquisition of Alliance Financial Corporation in 2005, which formed Alliance Financial Statutory Trust I ("Alliance Trust"). The Company also assumed additional debentures as the result of the acquisition of American Trust & Savings Bank ("American") in 2010, which formed Am Tru Statutory Trust I ("Am Tru Trust"). The Company also assumed additional debentures as the result of the Heartland transaction, which formed Heartland (IN) Statutory Trust II ("Heartland Trust"). In 2016, the Company also assumed additional debentures as the result of the LaPorte Bancorp transaction. LaPorte Bancorp acquired City Savings Financial Corporation in 2007. City Savings Financial Corporation issued the debentures and formed City Savings Statutory Trust I ("City Savings") in 2003. The Company also assumed additional debentures as the result of the Salin transaction, which formed Salin Statutory Trust I ("Salin Trust") in 2003. See Note 13 of the Consolidated Financial Statements included at Item 8 for further discussion regarding these previously consolidated entities that are now reported separately.

The business of Horizon is not seasonal to any material degree. No material part of Horizon's business is dependent upon a single or small group of customers, the loss of any one or more of which would have a materially adverse effect on the business of Horizon. In 2025, revenues from loans accounted for 291.4% of the total consolidated revenue, including the realized losses related to the balance sheet repositioning, and revenues from investment securities accounted for 42.9% of total consolidated revenue.

The Company's Internet address is www.horizonbank.com. Information on or accessible through our website is not deemed to be incorporated into this Annual Report on Form 10–K. Website references in this Annual Report are

merely textual references. The Company makes available, free of charge through the "About Us – Investor Relations – Documents – SEC Filings" section of its Internet website, copies of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10–K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10–Q, Current Reports on Form 8–K and any amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act"), as soon as reasonably practicable after those reports are filed with or furnished to the SEC. The contents of our website are not incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10–K or in any other report or document we file with the SEC, and any references to our website are intended to be inactive textual references only.

We believe that the foundation of our success in the banking business lies with the quality of our employees, the development of our employees' skills and career goals, and our ability to provide a comprehensive rewarding experience and work environment. We encourage and support the development of our employees and, wherever possible, strive to fill positions from within the organization.
As of December 31, 2025, the Company employed 465 full–time and 26 part–time employees across all locations.

Horizon faces a high degree of competition in all of its primary markets. The Bank's primary market consists of areas throughout the northern and central regions of the state of Indiana along with the southern and central regions of the state of Michigan. The Bank's primary market is further defined by the Indiana and Michigan counties identified below. The Bank competes with other commercial banks, savings and loan associations, consumer finance companies, credit unions and other non–bank and digital financial service providers. In addition, Financial Technology, or FinTech, start–ups are emerging in key banking areas. To a more moderate extent, the Bank competes with Chicago money center banks, mortgage banking companies, insurance companies, brokerage houses, other institutions engaged in money market financial services and certain government agencies. Many non–financial institution competitors face fewer regulatory restrictions.

headings: Our commercial, residential mortgage and consumer loans expose us to increased credit risks.
Our holdings of construction, land and home equity loans may pose more credit risk than other types of mortgage loans.
The allowance for credit losses on loans may prove inadequate or be negatively affected by credit risk exposures.
Changes in interest rates could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
We are exposed to intangible asset risk in that our goodwill may become impaired.
Our mortgage lending profitability could be significantly reduced as changes in interest rates could affect mortgage origination volume and pricing for selling mortgages on the secondary market.
The price of our common stock may fluctuate significantly, and this may make it difficult for you to resell our common stock at times or at prices you find attractive.
The trading volume in our common stock is less than that of other larger financial institutions.
We are subject to liquidity risk in our operations, which could adversely affect the ability to fund various obligations.
Unrealized losses in our investment portfolio could adversely affect liquidity.
We may need to raise additional capital in the future, and such capital may not be available when needed or at all.
Our internal controls may be ineffective, circumvented, or fail.
Our information systems may experience cyber–attacks or an interruption or breach in security. Our cybersecurity systems could be inadequate or fail.
Acts of terrorism or war, as well as the threat of terrorism or war, may adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition, and liquidity.
Pandemics, other global or regional health crises or disease outbreaks, natural disasters, global climate change, acts of terrorism and global conflicts may have a negative impact on our business.
The preparation of our financial statements requires the use of estimates that may vary from actual results.
Our remaining indirect lending exposures are subject to higher fraud risk than our other lending operations.
Due to the development of new technologies and regulatory actions encouraging the use of these technologies, consumers may decide not to use banks to complete their financial transactions.
We rely on other companies to provide key components of our business infrastructure.
The loss of key members of our senior management team and our lending teams could affect our ability to operate effectively.
Our inability to continue to process large volumes of transactions accurately could adversely impact our business and financial results.
Potential acquisitions may disrupt our business and dilute stockholder value.
An economic slowdown in our primary market areas could affect our business.

Negative developments affecting the banking industry, and resulting media coverage, may erode customer confidence in the banking system and could have a material effect on our operations and/or stock price.
The soundness of other financial institutions could adversely affect us.

Instability in global economic conditions and geopolitical matters, as well as volatility in financial markets, could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.
Any regulatory examination scrutiny or new regulatory requirements in the banking industry could increase the Company's expenses and affect the Company's operations.
We may be exposed to risk of environmental liabilities with respect to real property to which we take title.
We are subject to extensive regulation and changes in laws and regulatory policies could adversely affect our business.
Digital asset trends introduce regulatory and competitive challenges.
Provisions in our articles of incorporation, our by–laws, and Indiana law may delay or prevent an acquisition of us by a third party.
paragraphs: An investment in Horizon's securities is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties related to our business. The material risks and uncertainties that management believes currently affect Horizon are described below, categorized as risks related to our business, risks related to the banking industry generally, and risks related to our common stock. Additional risks and uncertainties that management is not aware of or that management currently deems immaterial may also impair Horizon's business operations and its financial results. This report is qualified in its entirety by these risk factors. If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. If this were to happen, the value of our securities could decline significantly, and you could lose all or part of your investment. As a result, before making an investment
decision, you should carefully consider these risks as well as information we include or incorporate by reference in this report and other filings we make with the SEC.
Some statements in the following risk factors constitute forward–looking statements. Please refer to "Forward–Looking Statements" beginning on page 3 of this Annual Report on Form 10–K.

As a financial institution, we are subject to a number of risks relating to our daily business. Although we undertake a variety of efforts to manage and control those risks, many of the risks are outside of our control. Among the risks we face are the following:
•Credit Risk – the risk that loan customers or other parties will be unable to perform their contractual obligations;
•Market Risk – the risk that changes in market rates and prices will adversely affect our financial condition or results of operation;

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025. We make statements in this section that are forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. All of such forward-looking statements are expressly qualified by reference to the cautionary statements provided under the caption "Forward-Looking Statements" included on page 3 of this report. Furthermore, a number of known and unknown factors may cause our actual results, performance or achievements to differ materially from those expressed or implied by the following discussion. Therefore, you are encouraged to read in its entirety the information provided under the caption "Risk Factors" included under Item 1A in Part I of this report for a discussion of risk factors that may negatively impact our expected results, performance, or achievements discussed below.

Horizon is a registered bank holding company incorporated in Indiana and headquartered in Michigan City, Indiana. Horizon provides a broad range of banking services in northern and central Indiana and southern and central Michigan through its bank subsidiary, Horizon Bank. Horizon operates as a single segment, which is commercial banking. Horizon's common stock is traded on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol HBNC. The Bank was founded in 1873 as a national association, and it remained a national association until its conversion to an Indiana commercial bank effective June 23, 2017. The Bank is a full–service commercial bank offering commercial and retail banking services, corporate and individual trust and agency services, and other services incident to banking.

•Strong performance of the core community banking model, combined with the successful completion of the balance sheet repositioning efforts, resulted in significant performance improvement for the quarter. The Company's return on average assets and return on average equity improved to 1.63% and 15.71%, respectively.

•Net interest income of $63.5 million for the three months ended December 31, 2025 increased 8.7% compared with $58.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, and 19.5% compared with $53.1 million in the year ago period. The net interest margin, on a fully taxable equivalent ("FTE") basis1, expanded for the ninth consecutive quarter, to 4.29% for the three months ended December 31, 2025, compared with 3.52% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 and 2.97% for the three months ended December 31, 2024.

•Total loans held for investment ("HFI") increased 4.4% as of December 31, 2025 compared to the linked quarter annualized, with strong organic commercial loan growth of $75.8 million, or 9.1% annualized.

•Funding costs continued to trend favorably. Non-interest bearing deposits balances remained relatively flat, while declines in interest-bearing balances largely reflected the communicated planned exit of high-cost, transactional deposits. Total interest-bearing liability costs decreased by another 34 bps during the quarter.

•Credit quality remained strong, with annualized net charge offs of 0.08% of average loans during the fourth quarter. Non-performing assets remain well within expected ranges, with non-performing assets to total assets of 63 bps for the fourth quarter.

•Expenses were comparable to the third quarter when considering a select few items related to the balance sheet activities, displaying management's continued commitment to generate positive operating leverage through a more efficient expense base.
1 Non-GAAP financial metric. See non-GAAP reconciliation included herein for the most directly comparable GAAP measure.
(Table dollars in thousands except per share data)

•Net interest income increased to $229.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $188.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, driven by net interest margin expansion, as average earning asset balances declined year-over-year as a result of the balance sheet repositioning efforts during Q3 2025. The net interest margin, on a fully taxable equivalent ("FTE")1 basis, expanded to 3.49% compared with 2.68% for the year ended December 31, 2024.

•The increase in FTE net interest margin was also driven by the Company's balance sheet repositioning in Q3 2025, which resulted in a shift of the Company's earning asset mix towards higher yielding commercial loans and funding mix toward relationship-based deposit funding, in addition to favorable trends loan yields and interest-bearing deposit costs. The asset mix shift was a result of an increase in its overall average loan balances of $226.5 million or 4.8%, from $4.7 billion for the year ended December 31, 2024 to $4.9 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025, while average balances of investment securities declined by $779.4 million, or 32.1%, to $1.6 billion from $2.4 billion in the same period a year ago.

•As discussed above, the Company repositioned the investment securities portfolio during Q3 2025. The Company reclassified its held-to-maturity investment portfolio, with a carrying value of $1.8 billion and unrealized loss of $282.6 million, to the available-for-sale portfolio as part of the Company's balance sheet repositioning. Following the reclassification, the Company sold securities with a fair value of $1.4 billion, recognizing a pre-tax loss of $299.5 million, with a portion of the net proceeds reallocated back into the securities portfolio. As a result, the yield of the Company's investment portfolio increased 52 bps to 2.87% for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 2.35% for the year ended December 31, 2024.

•Total loans, including loans held-for-sale, were $4.89 billion at December 31, 2025, down $28.3 million from December 31, 2024 balances, or (0.6)% year over year. Strong commercial loan growth of $354.3 million, or 11.5%, was offset by the sale of the mortgage warehouse portfolio in Q1 2025 and the indirect auto portfolio of $284.2 million during the Q3 2025.

paragraphs: 本節所述資訊受下列資訊之限制，包括本節 1A 項「風險因素」及 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」，以及本年度 10-K 報告其他處所列之警示聲明。

Horizon Bancorp, Inc.（"Horizon" 或 "本公司"）為一註冊的銀行控股公司，設立於印第安那州，總部位於印第安那州米基城。Horizon 透過其銀行子公司 Horizon Bank（"Horizon Bank" 或 "銀行"）及其他相關機構，在印第安那州北部及中部，以及密歇根州南部及中部提供廣泛的銀行服務。Horizon 以單一應報告分部營運，該分部為商業銀行。本公司普通股於 NASDAQ Global Select Market 交易，代碼為 HBNC。Horizon Bank（原稱 "Horizon Bank, N.A."）於 1873 年成立為全國性銀行協會，並持續為全國性銀行協會直至 2017 年 6 月 23 日轉為印第安那州商業銀行。該銀行為一家全功能商業銀行，提供商業及零售銀行服務、企業及個人信託與代理服務及其他與銀行相關服務。
過去 20 年來，Horizon 透過內生擴張與收購合併，擴大其地理範圍並實現財務成長。Horizon 最初的營運範圍集中於西北印第安那州，但自那之後，本公司已在密歇根州南部及中部，以及東北及中部印第安那州建立新的市場據點。

該銀行擁有 71 間全功能分行。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，該銀行總資產為 6.4 十億美元，總存款為 5.3 十億美元。該銀行擁有 100% 直接及間接子公司：Horizon Investments, Inc.（"Horizon Investments"）、Horizon Properties, Inc.（"Horizon Properties"）、Horizon Insurance Services, Inc.（"Horizon Insurance"）、Horizon Grantor Trust 及 Wolverine Commercial Holdings, LLC。Horizon Investments 管理該銀行的投資組合。Horizon Properties 管理不動產投資信託。Horizon Insurance 由本公司財富管理部門用以透過第三方銷售特定人壽保險產品。Horizon Grantor Trust 持有本公司所有之人壽保險契約。Wolverine Commercial Holdings, LLC 目前僅持有其中一處不動產，但不從事其他重大商業活動。

Horizon 於 2004 年成立 Horizon Bancorp Capital Trust II（"Trust II"），並於 2006 年成立 Horizon Bancorp Capital Trust III（"Trust III"），目的是參與集合信託優先受益證券發行。本公司因收購 Alliance Financial Corporation 而取得額外的可轉換債券，此交易形成 Alliance Financial Statutory Trust I（"Alliance Trust"）。本公司亦因收購 American Trust & Savings Bank（"American"）而取得額外的可轉換債券，此交易形成 Am Tru Statutory Trust I（"Am Tru Trust"）。本公司亦因 Heartland 交易而取得額外的可轉換債券，此交易形成 Heartland (IN) Statutory Trust II（"Heartland Trust"）。2016 年，本公司亦因 LaPorte Bancorp 交易而取得額外的可轉換債券。LaPorte Bancorp 於 2007 年收購 City Savings Financial Corporation。City Savings Financial Corporation 發行可轉換債券並於 2003 年成立 City Savings Statutory Trust I（"City Savings"）。本公司亦因 Salin 交易而取得額外的可轉換債券，此交易形成 Salin Statutory Trust I（"Salin Trust"）於 2003 年成立。請參閱第 8 項所附之合併財務報表附註 13，以進一步瞭解這些已合併但現已分開報告之先前合併實體。
Horizon 之業務並無明顯季節性。本公司業務並無依賴單一或小組客戶，若失去其中任一或數個客戶，對本公司業務將不會造成重大不利影響。2025 年，貸款收入佔總合併營收的 291.4%，包含因資產重組所產生之實現損失，投資證券收入佔總合併營收的 42.9%。
本公司網站地址為 www.horizonbank.com。網站上之資訊並未被視為納入本年度 10-K 報告。本年度 10-K 報告中之網站參考僅為文字參考。

僅為文字參考。本公司透過其網際網路網站的 "About Us – Investor Relations – Documents – SEC Filings" 部分，免費提供本公司年度報告表 10–K、季報表 10–Q、現況報告表 8–K 及任何對這些報告之更正文件，這些文件係根據 1934 年證券交易法第 13(a) 節（"Exchange Act"）之規定，於這些報告提交或提供給 SEC 後儘可能迅速提供。本公司網站之內容並未被引用為本年度報告表 10–K 或任何其他提交至 SEC 之報告或文件之部分，任何提及本公司網站之參考係僅為無效文字參考。
我們認為，在銀行業務中取得成功的基礎，係建立於員工的素質、員工技能與職業目標的發展，以及我們提供全面且具報酬的經驗與工作環境之能力。我們鼓勵並支持員工的發展，並在可能的情況下，努力從組織內部補充職缺。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司於所有營運據點總計僱用465名全職與26名兼職員工。

Horizon在所有主要市場面臨高度競爭。銀行的主要市場包括印第安那州北部與中部地區，以及密歇根州南部與中部地區。銀行的主要市場進一步以下列印第安那州與密歇根州的縣為界定。銀行與其他商業銀行、儲蓄貸款協會、消費者金融公司、信用合作社及其他非銀行與數位金融服務提供者競爭。此外，金融科技，或FinTech，新創公司正在關鍵銀行領域興起。在較為程度上，銀行與芝加哥錢中心銀行、房貸銀行公司、保險公司、證券經紀公司、其他從事貨幣市場金融服務的機構與某些政府機構競爭。許多非金融機構的競爭對手面對較少的監管限制。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析應與本年度年報 10-K 表單中所包含之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀，該財務報表及附註載於本年報其他部分，為截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之財務年度。本節中我們所作之陳述係根據聯邦證券法之含義所屬之向前看陳述。所有上述向前看陳述皆明確引用本報告第 3 頁所載之警示陳述為準。此外，若干已知及未知因素可能導致我們實際之結果、表現或成就與以下討論所表達或暗示者有重大差異。因此，您被鼓勵完整閱讀本報告第一部分第 1A 項所載之 "風險因素" 節，以瞭解可能對以下所討論之預期結果、表現或成就產生負面影響之風險因素。

Horizon為一註冊之銀行控股公司，於印第安那州註冊，總部設於印第安那州米切爾城。Horizon透過其銀行子公司Horizon Bank，在印第安那州北部及中部，以及密歇根州南部及中部提供廣泛之銀行服務。Horizon運作為單一應報告分部，該分部為商業銀行。Horizon之普通股於NASDAQ Global Select Market交易，代碼為HBNC。該銀行於1873年成立為國家協會，並持續為國家協會直至2017年6月23日轉為印第安那州商業銀行。該銀行為一全功能商業銀行，提供商業及零售銀行服務、企業及個人信託與代理服務，以及其他與銀行相關之服務。
•核心社區銀行模式之強勁表現，結合資產負債表重新定位之成功完成，導致本季度有顯著之績效改善。本公司之資產平均回報率及權益平均回報率分別提高至1.63%及15.71%。
•截至2025年12月31日之總貸款（"HFI"）較前一個季度年化成長4.4%，其中強勁之內生性商業貸款成長為75.8 百萬美元，或年化成長9.1%。
•資金成本持續呈現有利趨勢。非利息產生存款餘額維持相對穩定，而利息產生存款餘額之減少主要反映已通報之高成本交易性存款計畫退出。本季度總利息產生負債成本再減少34 bps。
•信用品質維持強勁，第四季年化淨核銷率為平均貸款之0.08%。非營運資產仍遠低於預期範圍，第四季非營運資產佔總資產之比為63 bps。
•費用與第三季相比大致相當，考量若干與資產負債表活動相關之項目，顯示管理層持續致力於透過更有效率之費用基礎產生正向營運槓桿。
1 非GAAP財務指標。請參閱本文件內所附之非GAAP項目與最接近之GAAP衡量標準之對應說明。
(表格金額以千美元為單位，每股資料除外)
•淨利息收入增至2025年12月31日財年為229.5百萬美元，較2024年12月31日財年之188.6百萬美元增加，主要因淨利息邊際擴張，由於在2025年第三季進行資產負債表重新定位後，平均獲利資產餘額較去年同期下降。以完全課稅等效（"FTE"）1為基礎的淨利息邊際擴張至3.49%，較2024年12月31日財年之2.68%增加。

•FTE淨利息邊際的增加也因本公司在2025年第三季進行資產負債表重新定位，導致本公司獲利資產組成向高收益率的商業貸款轉移，以及資金組成向基於關係的存款資金轉移，加上貸款收益率及利息負擔存款成本的有利趨勢。資產組成的轉移是因本公司整體平均貸款餘額增加226.5百萬美元或4.8%，從2024年12月31日財年之47億美元增至2025年12月31日財年之49億美元，同時平均投資證券餘額減少779.4百萬美元，或32.1%，降至16億美元，較去年同期24億美元下降。

•如上所述，本公司在2025年第三季重新定位投資證券組合。本公司將其持有至到期投資組合，帳面價值為18億美元，未實現損失為282.6百萬美元，重新分類至可供出售組合，作為本公司資產負債表重新定位的一部分。重新分類後，本公司出售了帳面價值為14億美元的證券，認列預稅損失299.5百萬美元，部分淨現金重新投入證券組合。因此，本公司投資組合的收益率提高52個基點，至2025年12月31日財年為2.87%，較2024年12月31日財年之2.35%增加。

與我們業務相關的風險
我們的商業、住宅房貸及消費貸款使我們面臨更高的信用風險。
我們持有建設、土地及房屋 equity 貸款的資產，可能比其他類型的房貸貸款具有更高的信用風險。
貸款的信用損失撥備可能不足，或因信用風險敞口而受到負面影響。
利率的變動可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們面臨無形資產風險，因為我們的商譽可能發生減值。
我們的房貸貸款獲利可能因利率變動而大幅下降，影響房貸發放量及在二級市場出售房貸的定價。
本公司普通股之價格可能大幅波動，此情形可能使您在特定時機或以您認為具吸引力之價格出售本公司普通股變得困難。
本公司普通股之交易量低於其他較大型金融機構之交易量。
本公司在營運過程中可能面臨流動性風險，此風險可能不利於履行各項義務之資金籌措能力。
投資組閤中未實現之損失可能不利於流動性。
本公司未來可能需要籌措額外資金，而所需資金可能在需要時無法取得或完全無法取得。
本公司內部控制制度可能無法有效運作、遭繞過或失效。
本公司資訊系統可能遭遇網路攻擊或中斷或安全漏洞。本公司網路安全系統可能不足或失效。
恐怖攻擊或戰爭行為，以及恐怖攻擊或戰爭的威脅，可能對本公司營運成果、財務狀況及流動性產生不利影響。
疫情、其他全球或區域性健康危機或疾病爆發、天然災害、全球氣候變遷、恐怖攻擊及全球衝突可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司財務報表的編製需使用估計數，這些估計數可能與實際結果不同。
本公司剩餘間接貸款 exposures 可能面臨較高詐欺風險，與本公司其他貸款業務相比。
由於新技術的發展及監管機構鼓勵使用這些技術的措施，消費者可能決定不使用銀行完成其財務交易。
本公司依賴其他公司提供業務基礎設施的關鍵零組件。
本公司高階管理團隊及貸款團隊的重要成員離職，可能影響本公司有效營運的能力。
本公司無法持續準確處理大量交易之能力，可能對本公司業務及財務結果產生不利影響。
潛在之併購可能幹擾本公司業務，並稀釋股東價值。
本公司主要市場區域之經濟減速可能影響本公司業務。
影響銀行業之負面發展，以及相關媒體報導，可能削弱客戶對銀行體系之信心，並可能對本公司營運及/或股票價格產生重大影響。
其他金融機構之健全性可能對本公司產生不利影響。
全球經濟情勢不穩定及國際政治事務，以及金融市場之波動性，可能對本公司營運結果及財務狀況產生重大不利影響。

paragraphs: 投資 Horizon 之證券將面臨與我們業務相關之多重風險與不確定性。管理階層認為目前影響 Horizon 之重大風險與不確定性，已於下文敘述，分為與我們業務相關之風險、與銀行業一般相關之風險，以及與我們普通股相關之風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，管理階層尚未知悉或目前認為不重要，也可能影響 Horizon 之業務運作及其財務結果。本報告全部內容均受這些風險因素之限制。若任何下列風險實際發生，將可能對我們之業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成重大且不利之影響。若發生此情況，我們之證券價值可能顯著下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。因此，在做出投資決定前，您應謹慎考量這些風險，以及我們於本報告中所包含或援引之資訊，以及其他向 SEC 提交之申報文件。
下列風險因素中，部分陳述屬未來展望性陳述。請參閱本年度報告表 10-K 第 3 頁開始之「未來展望性陳述」部分。
Some statements in the following risk factors constitute forward–looking statements. Please refer to "Forward–Looking Statements" beginning on page 3 of this Annual Report on Form 10–K.
作為一家金融機構，我們面臨許多與日常業務相關的風險。雖然我們致力於管理及控制這些風險，但許多風險是我們無法控制的。我們所面臨的風險包括以下各項：
•信用風險 – 借款客戶或其他當事人無法履行契約義務的風險；
•市場風險 – 市場利率與價格的變動可能對我們的財務狀況或營運成果產生負面影響的風險；
